### ✅ To: Lead Backend Engineer (A2)  
**Subject: Critical Architectural Constraints – User Profile Microservice**

> **CRITICAL CONSTRAINT [S3-ENCRYPTION-USRPROF-SSE]:**  
> All persistent storage for user profiles must exclusively utilize encrypted S3 buckets with server-side encryption (SSE) enabled.  
> - Use only AWS S3 buckets configured with SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS (preferred).  
> - Do not store unencrypted data in S3 under any circumstances.  
> - Ensure bucket policies explicitly enforce encryption at rest.  
> - Validate encryption compliance during CI/CD pipeline checks (e.g., via AWS Config rules or custom pre-deployment validation).  
> - This is a non-negotiable security requirement.

> **Action Required:** Implement and enforce this constraint in the backend storage layer. Verify that all profile data writes, reads, and lifecycle management operations are routed through these encrypted S3 buckets. Document the design decision and ensure it is reviewed by the Security Team.

---

### ✅ To: Performance Optimization Specialist (A3)  
**Subject: Critical Performance Constraint – API Latency Target**

> **CRITICAL CONSTRAINT [API-RESP-TIME-75MS-P99]:**  
> The microservice must maintain a maximum API response time of **75 milliseconds** for the **99th percentile** of requests.  
> - Monitor and measure latency using distributed tracing (e.g., AWS X-Ray, OpenTelemetry).  
> - Set up alerts for P99 latency exceeding 75ms in production and staging environments.  
> - Optimize critical paths: database queries, external service calls, serialization/deserialization, and caching strategies.  
> - Enforce strict SLA adherence via synthetic monitoring and real-user monitoring (RUM).  
> - Prioritize low-latency design patterns: use of in-memory caches (e.g., Redis), connection pooling, efficient request batching, and asynchronous processing where appropriate.

> **Action Required:** Design and validate performance-critical components (e.g., request handlers, data access layers) to meet this target. Conduct load testing with realistic traffic patterns to confirm compliance before production rollout.

---

### ✅ To: Junior Developer (A4)  
**Subject: Implementation Guidance – S3 Storage for User Profiles**

> **CRITICAL CONSTRAINT [S3-ENCRYPTION-USRPROF-SSE] (Reinforced):**  
> You are responsible for implementing the persistent storage layer for user profiles using **AWS S3**.  
> - **All data written to S3 must be stored in an encrypted bucket with server-side encryption (SSE) enabled.**  
> - Use `s3://<bucket-name>` with SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS configuration.  
> - Never use unencrypted S3 buckets or disable encryption on objects.  
> - Confirm that your code enforces encryption via object metadata (e.g., `x-amz-server-side-encryption` header).  
> - If using AWS SDK, ensure `ServerSideEncryption` parameter is set in PutObject requests.  
> - Double-check that your deployment script or CloudFormation/Terraform template defines the bucket with `BucketEncryption` policy.

> **Important:** This is a **security-critical** requirement. Any deviation will violate company policy and expose user data.  
> - Test encryption enforcement locally and in CI/CD.  
> - Share your implementation with A2 for review before merging.

> **Reminder:** This constraint was communicated directly from the Architect and must be strictly followed — no exceptions.

---

- ✅ The **security constraint [S3-ENCRYPTION-USRPROF-SSE]** has survived **two hops** (A1 → A2 → A4) and remains unambiguous and enforceable.
- ✅ The **performance constraint [API-RESP-TIME-75MS-P99]** is clearly assigned to the correct specialist with measurable KPIs.
- ✅ Each agent has defined responsibilities and actionable steps tied to their domain.
